title: Names of geological time

paragraphs.text: Geologists divide Earth's history into nested units of time. From largest to smallest they are eons, eras, periods, epochs and ages. The tabs on this book's foredge mark the eras (the Hadean, which has no eras, has one tab for the whole eon); the running head at the top of each page names every unit the page begins in.

The boundaries are set by the International Commission on Stratigraphy. In the Phanerozoic most are pinned to a reference level in a particular section of rock, a Global Boundary Stratotype Section and Point or “golden spike”. The earlier boundaries are round-number ages adopted in 1990, placed between major cycles of sedimentation, mountain building and magmatism but not tied to any body of rock. The only Precambrian golden spike marks the base of the Ediacaran Period, 635 million years ago. The start of the Hadean is informal: it is taken as the age of the Solar System's first solids.

rows.meaning: After Hades, the Greek underworld. Preston Cloud's name (1972) for the time from the Earth's formation to the oldest confidently dated rocks.
Greek for “early life”; named by S. F. Emmons in 1888.
Greek for “visible life”: the eon of abundant fossils.
“Old life”. One of John Phillips's three great periods of past life (1841).
